title: Proposal: Declarative dependent form controls (conditional inputs without scripting)
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?


# Proposal: Declarative dependent form controls (conditional inputs without scripting)

---

## Problem

HTML currently has no declarative mechanism for expressing *conditional* form fields — i.e., fields that should be enabled only when a particular radio button, checkbox, or select option is chosen.  
This creates a very common pattern that cannot be implemented without JavaScript.

Examples of patterns that cannot be expressed declaratively today:

- “Other (please specify): [text]”
- “If yes, give details: [textarea]”
- “Specify custom amount: [number]”
- “When selecting ‘custom date’, enable: [date]”
- “Provide supporting document: [file input]”

Because browsers do not support this natively, authors must implement:

- enable/disable logic  
- show/hide behaviour  
- labelling associations  
- ARIA relationships  
- ensuring inaccessible or inactive fields cannot receive focus  
- ensuring inactive fields are not submitted  

Implementations vary widely and often have accessibility issues.

This is a very common pattern across surveys, government forms, checkout flows, medical questionnaires, registrations, etc. The use-case is strong and universal.

---

## Proposal

Introduce an attribute (placeholder name: `controls`) that establishes a declarative dependency between a *controlling* element (radio, checkbox, or select/option) and a *dependent* element (any non-choice input field).

### Controlling elements
- `<input type="radio">`  
- `<input type="checkbox">`  
- `<option>` within `<select>`  

### Dependent elements (allowed)

Any of:

- `<input type="text">`  
- `<input type="email">`  
- `<input type="tel">`  
- `<input type="url">`  
- `<input type="password">`  
- `<input type="number">`  
- `<input type="range">`  
- `<input type="date">`  
- `<input type="time">`  
- `<input type="month">`  
- `<input type="week">`  
- `<input type="datetime-local">`  
- `<input type="color">`  
- `<input type="file">`  
- `<textarea>`  

**Explicitly excluded** (not valid dependent fields):

- `<input type="radio">`  
- `<input type="checkbox">`  
- `<input type="search">`  
- `<select>`  
- `<output>`  

*(These exclusions prevent nested-choice constructs and maintain clear semantics.)*

---

## Proposed behaviour

If the controlling element is not selected (radio/option) or unchecked (checkbox):

- The dependent element is disabled  
- It must not receive focus  
- It must not be submitted  
- Assistive technologies should be informed through appropriate ARIA exposure  

If the controlling element becomes selected/checked:

- The dependent element becomes enabled  
- It may be **revealed visually** (for example, hidden until enabled, or grayed out until selected)  
- It becomes focusable  
- It is included in form submission  

This behaviour **does not break existing form semantics**, since only disabled fields are excluded from submission; all non-disabled fields continue to be submitted as usual.

---

## Examples

### 1. Radio button enabling a text field

```html
<input type="radio" name="food" value="other" controls="food_other">
<input type="text" id="food_other" placeholder="Please specify">
```

### 2. Checkbox enabling a date field

```html
<input type="checkbox" id="choose_date" controls="date_custom">
<input type="date" id="date_custom">
```

### 3. Select option enabling a number field

```html
<select name="height">
  <option value="preset1">Standard Height</option>
  <option value="preset2">Tall</option>
  <option value="custom" controls="height_custom">Custom Height</option>
</select>

<input type="number" id="height_custom" min="1" max="300">
```

---

## Accessibility considerations

This proposal would:

- eliminate many inaccessible JS implementations  
- ensure inactive fields cannot be focused  
- ensure screen readers properly understand dependency relationships  
- create predictable, interoperable semantics across browsers  
- reduce scripting that overrides UA focus/keyboard behaviour  

A new ARIA mapping could be defined, or existing relationships could be reused.

---

## Non-goals

- This does *not* create nested or composite input types.  
- This does *not* allow dependent choice controls (radio/checkbox/select).  
- This does *not* attempt to standardise visual presentation beyond the “may be revealed” guidance.  
- This does *not* replace custom web-component solutions; it provides a baseline native mechanism.

---

## Why this belongs in HTML

- The use-case occurs in virtually every non-trivial form.  
- Authors currently rely on hand-rolled JS and inconsistent accessibility patterns.  
- Browsers can handle this more safely, consistently, and accessibly than scripted solutions.  
- This aligns with HTML’s goal of providing declarative primitives for common form behaviour.
